blockers.summary: The Phase 51 consumer payment gate is bypassable by the participant it charges.
blockers.detail: RLS on consumer_briefcase_items is owner-scoped but restricts no column, and nothing in supabase/ revokes or triggers on payment_status or amount_cents. On default Supabase privileges, authenticated holds column-level UPDATE on payment_status: a participant can mark their own row paid/5000, or insert a row already marked paid with no checkout, and finalization then returns zero_charge/eligible. The delivery route's ownership check does not help because the forger owns the item.
blockers.reproduced: Independently on an ephemeral cluster at this tip: 13/17 gate cases pass, 4 fail (G1, G1b critical; G11, G12 high). Mutations 3/3 behaved as expected.
blockers.alsoFound: G11 — the consumption unit is keyed on job id, so one $50 purchase authorizes unlimited packets across unlimited matters, and the ledger uniqueness index excludes zero_charge entirely. G12 — the gate does not compare the item's user_id to the job's participant at the database layer; enqueue being service_role-only and the delivery ownership check mitigate this at the route layer, but the database does not enforce it.
blockers.fixture: scripts/verify-rcap-phase51-consumer-payment-security.mjs (exits non-zero while the four expectations fail)
blockers.recommendation: docs/RCAP_PHASE51_CONSUMER_PAYMENT_SECURITY.md carries two patches, both validated on the audit cluster, including the caveat that the second must catch unique_violation and return a typed result rather than raise, or a rejected redemption rolls back the artifact evidence and strands the job in validating.
blockers.requiresAuthorization: Yes. A fix means a new file under supabase/ and touches RLS/privileges, both of which need Roger's explicit authorization before they are written or applied. Not taken unilaterally.
blockers.consequence: Applying 49+50+51 to staging today would deploy a payment gate that a paying participant can defeat. Phase 51 still fixes the regression it was written for; it does not survive a hostile payer.

repositoryRemediation.evidence: verify-rcap-phase52-consumer-payment-authority 32/32; test-rcap-phase52-mutations 12/12; G1, G1b, G11 and G12 re-run and closed
repositoryRemediation.whyStillUnresolved: The fix exists in the repository and is proven against an ephemeral cluster. It is not applied to any environment: staging and production are both queued and no environment has been named. A finding is resolved when the environment it describes is fixed, not when a migration that would fix it is merged.

supersededStagingAction.was: Apply phases 49, 50 and 51 to staging in one authorized window.
supersededStagingAction.reason: Phase 51 as written is bypassable by the payer (RCAP-SEC-001, audit commit f82f842). Applying 49 -> 50 -> 51 to any environment that takes payment would ship the proven bypass, so the three-migration action must not be executed in that form. Phase 52 is additive and must be applied in the same window, which makes the action a four-migration one.

preparedStagingAction.note: Prepared, not requested. Roger must name all four migration files AND the staging environment before this becomes an authorization request. Nothing here executes itself, and preparing it authorizes nothing.
preparedStagingAction.indivisible: 51 and 52 must be applied in the same window. Applying 51 without 52 ships the proven bypass; applying 52 without 51 leaves the consumer branch ungated in the phase-50 shape. Neither half is a valid stopping point.
preparedStagingAction.applicationPrecondition: The consumer checkout path must already write payments through record_consumer_packet_payment. Phase 52 revokes the participant's ability to write payment facts, so any environment taking live payments with the old write path will capture money at the provider and fail to record it.
